subject: Energy
title: What Is a Smart Grid?
description: A fast breakdown of What Is a Smart Grid? for builders.

hook.text: A smart grid layers digital communication over the physical network—making electricity flow visible and controllable.

buildup.text: Sensors, smart meters, and automated switches feed data to control centers—enabling real-time monitoring everywhere.

discovery.text: Software optimizes power flows, predicts faults, and reroutes around problems—faster than any human operator.

twist.text: The traditional grid is 'blind' past the substation—operators often learn about outages from customer phone calls.

climax.text: Smart grids enable two-way power flow—rooftop solar, batteries, and EVs can feed energy back, not just consume it.

punchline.text: See everything, control everything—the grid gets a brain.

quiz.question: What enables two-way power flow on a smart grid?
